population: Every `#[test]` function under alacritty_terminal/src at the pinned commit. This is a different population from alacritty-manifest.json, which classifies the 45 alacritty_terminal/tests/ref recording directories; neither file describes the other's cases.

dispositions.adapted: A DanTerm test in `destination` tracks this scenario and cites this name.
dispositions.superseded: Reaches DanTerm behavior, but existing DanTerm tests already pin it at least as strongly. Porting would add a duplicate, not a boundary.
dispositions.implementation-coupled: Specifies Alacritty's internal representation. There is no DanTerm behavior underneath it.
dispositions.unsupported: Requires a feature DanTerm does not offer, or lives outside TerminalCore.
dispositions.policy-divergence: Reachable, but DanTerm's contract deliberately produces a different result. Adopting the verdict would mean adopting Alacritty's policy.

method: Adoption required more than 'the scenario is reachable': each retained case was checked to fail independently by mutating DanTerm and confirming that no existing test already caught the mutation. Candidates that survived that check are `adapted`; candidates whose mutations existing tests already caught are `superseded`, with the evidence recorded.

tests.rationale: Specifies Alacritty's rotating `Storage` vector -- its capacity, its zero-point rotation, and growth and truncation around that point. DanTerm stores rows in a plain array plus a scrollback deque, so there is no observable behavior under this test to port.
tests.evidence: DanTerm's row-storage claims are public: scrollbackRowCount, scrollbackRow(at:), and the budget/eviction behavior in TerminalScrollbackBudgetTests and TerminalScrollbackTests.

tests.rationale: Probed and rejected rather than assumed. The portable claim -- an unwritten cell between two written cells is text and survives reflow, while unwritten cells after the last written one never are -- holds in DanTerm, but a test asserting it cannot fail independently. Two mutations were injected to try: dropping unwritten cells in the reflow copy, and counting trailing padding as retained content. Existing tests caught both, so a fourth adapted test would have added a duplicate rather than a boundary.
tests.evidence: Dropping padding in reflow is caught by TerminalResizeTests#cellAnchorsFollowReflowedCells (which uses this exact interior-gap stimulus), #interleavedResizeAndInputPreservesValidGrid, and the selection-attachment case; counting trailing padding as content is caught by 20+ tests across the selection, viewport, resize, and prompt-anchor suites.

Specifies Alacritty's private selection endpoint arithmetic: which `Side` an endpoint sits on, and the inclusive `SelectionRange` that arithmetic produces. DanTerm exposes a half-open `TerminalTextRange` over the logical projection and has no endpoint-side concept, so translating these would encode a representation DanTerm rejected.
tests.evidence: TerminalSelectionTests asserts the observable consequences -- selected text, grapheme and wide-cell atomicity, and attachment across mutation -- through that public range.

tests.rationale: The one inline case that crosses two DanTerm subsystems no existing test crosses together: an in-place full-screen erase while the viewport is parked on retained history. Adopted as a regression guard -- DanTerm already behaves correctly, and a mutation making ED 2 reset browsing was caught by this test and by no other test in the suite.
tests.evidence: Mutation check: setting `viewportState = .following` in ED 2 failed exactly 1 of the 821 TerminalCore tests -- the adapted one. Re-confirmed after rebasing onto the reflow trailing-blank-cursor fix and the WezTerm adaptations.

tests.rationale: Its portable half is the same ED-2-preserves-the-viewport claim as its non-vi sibling, which is adapted; its distinct half asserts the vi cursor point, which DanTerm has no analogue for. Folding the portable half in would duplicate the sibling exactly.
tests.evidence: Covered by the adaptation of #clearing_viewport_keeps_history_position.

tests.rationale: Alacritty snaps the display back to the live bottom when ED 3 clears scrollback. DanTerm deliberately clamps the browsing anchor instead and keeps `isFollowing == false`, so that eviction never yanks a reading user to the prompt. Adopting the verdict would mean adopting Alacritty's interaction policy over DanTerm's.
tests.evidence: TerminalViewportTests#evictionClampsBrowsingAnchor pins DanTerm's contrary choice explicitly, including the ED 3 path.

tests.rationale: Requires Alacritty's in-emulator vi mode. DanTerm's interaction model is AppKit selection and local viewport browsing, and it does not offer a vi cursor, vi motions, or vi-mode scrolling.
tests.evidence: TerminalInteractionPolicyTests and TerminalSelectionTests cover DanTerm's actual interaction model.

tests.rationale: Asserts that after ED 3 the grid is unchanged by a scroll-to-top, via grid equality. DanTerm asserts the same idea publicly and more specifically: the scrollback row count, the projection anchor, and the retained text after ED 3.

tests.rationale: Half of this is covered: DanTerm decodes OSC title changes into semantic events and tests them, including coalescing, limits, UTF-8, and chunking. The other half is the CSI title stack (push/pop and its 4096-entry cap), a capability DanTerm has not decided to support. Whether to implement it is a feature decision that must precede any test port; a test cannot create the requirement.
tests.evidence: TerminalSemanticEventTests covers the decoded OSC title event seam.

tests.rationale: Reaches into `term.grid[..]` to plant a cell state -- a wide char with no spacer, or a spacer flag with no wide char -- that Alacritty's own parser never produces. The ground rules forbid constructing invalid private grid states to imitate an upstream fixture, and DanTerm's public byte feed cannot reach these states at all.
tests.evidence: DanTerm's spacer invariants are asserted structurally by expectValidGrid over every resize, erase, and fuzz test rather than probed from a hand-built grid.

tests.rationale: The only inline case that measures a search match range over a double-width grapheme. DanTerm already reports the correct two-column range, but nothing pinned it: a mutation making wide projection units report one column was caught only by the two adapted wide-search tests.
tests.evidence: Mutation check: narrowing wide projection units to one column failed exactly 2 of the 821 TerminalCore tests, both adapted. Re-confirmed after rebasing onto the reflow trailing-blank-cursor fix and the WezTerm adaptations.

tests.rationale: The wide-grapheme-at-a-line-break edge. Adapted with a changed stimulus: upstream builds two hard-separated rows, while DanTerm feeds one logical line and lets the width wrap it, so the test actually exercises the soft wrap and the padding column a pushed wide grapheme leaves behind.
tests.evidence: Same mutation check as #singlecell_fullwidth.

tests.rationale: A wide-grapheme search scenario in the same family as the two adapted wide cases -- a wide unit at a row end, at a soft wrap, or adjacent to a narrow one. Once the range covering a wide unit and the crossing of a wrap are pinned, these differ only in which side of the boundary the wide unit sits on.
tests.evidence: Covered by the adaptations of #singlecell_fullwidth and #wrapping_into_fullwidth in TerminalAlacrittyAdaptedTests, plus TerminalSelectionTests wide-atomicity cases.
